question: Who were most of the men officially honoured afterwards as conquerors of the Bastille?
answer: Craftsmen, journeymen and shopkeepers. George Rudé traced the trades of several hundred men on the official list: most were settled working people of the Faubourg Saint-Antoine, joiners, cabinet-makers, locksmiths and wine-sellers, beside a few dozen soldiers. Vagrants and the destitute barely appear. The crowd had addresses and trades.
move: Before believing a description of a crowd, ask who wrote it.
ask: Before I believe a description of a crowd, do I ask who wrote it?
trap: Imagining the crowd as a rabble of the destitute, as its enemies described it.
source: Rudé, The Crowd in the French Revolution, 1959
reference: Rudé, The Crowd in the French Revolution, Clarendon Press, 1959
